(I) IBC stations in Bombay and Calcutta (1927)
(II) Fielden establishes Delhi station (1936)
(III) Six-station domestic network at Partition (1947)
(IV) Launch of Vividh Bharati entertainment channel (1957)
(V) Commissioning of Chennai first FM service (1977)

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV -> V
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I -> V
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV -> V
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV -> V
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Expansion timeline: 1927 (Bombay/Calcutta) -> 1936 (Delhi) -> 1947 (Partition) -> 1957 (Vividh Bharati) -> 1977 (Chennai FM).
Hence, Option D is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

questionText:
Read the following case analysis on cinematic realism and Indian film history and answer the questions that follow:

In 1955, Satyajit Ray completed his directorial debut 'Pather Panchali' (Song of the Little Road), financed partly by a loan from the West Bengal government and pawned family jewelry. Screened at the 1956 Cannes Film Festival, the film stunned international critics and was awarded the prestigious 'Prix du Document Humain' (Best Human Document), catapulting Indian cinema onto the global auteur map. Adapted from Bibhutibhushan Bandopadhyay's novel, Pather Panchali revolutionized Indian film aesthetics. Rejecting the artificiality of Bombay film studios, painted sets, and formulaic song-and-dance interruptions, Ray embraced authentic Neo-Realism. He shot predominantly on location in the village of Boral, cast non-professional actors (including 80-year-old Chunibala Devi as the impoverished aunt Indir Thakrun), utilized natural available sunlight, and crafted iconic visual poetry—such as the breathless sequence of young Apu and Durga running through fields of swaying white Kash flowers to catch their first glimpse of a roaring steam railway train, scored to the brilliant sitar music of Pandit Ravi Shankar.

Question: Which prestigious award did Satyajit Ray's 'Pather Panchali' win at the 1956 Cannes Film Festival?

options.text: Prix du Document Humain (Best Human Document)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Golden Lion for Best Animated Film
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

questionText: Which of the following statements regarding Radio during Partition (1947) in Radio and Cinema is INCORRECT / NOT true?

options.text: It conforms strictly to the standard equilibrium conditions defined in NCERT Radio and Cinema.
options.mistakeAnalysis: This is a factually correct principle of NCERT and cannot be chosen as an incorrect statement.

options.text: It exhibits consistent and reproducible behavior across verified experimental measurements.
options.mistakeAnalysis: This is a factually correct principle of NCERT and cannot be chosen as an incorrect statement.

options.text: Its magnitude depends directly on the governing physical or analytical constants of Radio during Partition (1947).
options.mistakeAnalysis: This is a factually correct principle of NCERT and cannot be chosen as an incorrect statement.

options.text: It operates in direct violation of the fundamental conservation laws of Radio and Cinema.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Identifies the statement that contains a scientific falsehood.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to standard NCERT Radio and Cinema specifications, Radio during Partition (1947) is fully consistent with established principles and does not violate conservation laws.
Therefore, statement (D) is false, making it the correct answer to this negative constraint question.
